title: registry-v0 record — one curated YAML file per registered repository
description: The P-M2-only, PR-curated registry source of truth: one file `registry/{owner}--{name}.yml` in the public curated registry repository (FS-02 §7 FS02-060). THIS is the schema that repository validates against — it holds a byte-identical vendored copy and its CI fails on any byte difference, so there is one record contract rather than two that agree by habit. The filename is derived from `owner` and `name`, lowercased and joined by `--`, because an opaque `R_kgDO…` filename makes a curation pull request unreviewable at a glance; `node_id` remains the primary key in every artifact and every reference (FS-02 §7's `repos/{node_id}.yml` is the chapter's earlier form). Consumed by the index-build-lite job that renders the published artifacts (VS-04). Three hard constraints carry legal weight: (1) there is NO `waivers` field and there never will be — waivers are issued only by a claimed admin from the platform dashboard (D14), so no waiver can enter the registry by pull request; (2) the YAML file is a CACHE of display facts, while the repository's own committed LICENSE file is the truth about adoption (D13); (3) this whole repository is data class P0-public (FS-00 §6.9), so the only person-identifying data a record may hold is a GitHub login — the `contacts` patterns make an e-mail address structurally unrepresentable (D15). Frozen and archived at P-M3 with a pointer to the export endpoints (FS-00 §2).

consumers: the curated registry repository's validation CI (FS02-061)

schema.description: Record schema tag. A value this validator does not know must fail the pull request — a broken registry never half-publishes (FS02-063). Unlike `PURPOSE.yml`, which is optional overrides and degrades to defaults (D23), a registry record is the published cache of an adoption.

example.description: Marks a seeded demonstration record. `true` records exist so the tooling has data to run against; index-build-lite EXCLUDES them from every published artifact and CI fails if one leaks into the output. A real record omits the key entirely.

node_id.description: GitHub GraphQL node_id — the primary key everywhere (FS-00 §6.1, GH-003); `owner`/`name` are display cache only and appear in no key. Existence cannot be validated at v0 (P-M2 §4.2 edge case 4).

owner.description: Owner login. DISPLAY CACHE ONLY — refreshed by the operator on a rename; never a key, never money-bearing (FS02-017).

name.description: Repository name. Display cache only. Also the shard key for the published registry index (first character, FS02-062). Leading dots and the reserved names `.`/`..` are excluded because they would produce an unusable filename.

default_branch.description: Default branch at the time of curation (FS02-010). Used only to build human links; a stale value never affects registration.

state.description: The FS-02 §3 state enum verbatim. `detected` repositories appear in aggregate counts only — no listing, no repo record, no badge (GH-014). `powers_suspended` and `allocation_frozen` are the two orthogonal private flags of FS02-020 and are deliberately absent from this contract: they are platform state, never registry data.

state_note.description: Optional short public reason CLASS shown on the neutral tombstone page for `delisted`/`quit` (WEB-075). A reason class, not a narrative, and never a person's name. Required in practice for those two states, which a validator expresses better than a schema.

license.description: The adopted licence version and the evidence for it. The repository's own LICENSE file is the source of truth for adoption (GH-002, LEG-027 as amended, D13); these fields are the cache of what the operator verified.

id.description: Identifier of the adopted licence version. `PurposeSource-1.0` is the working form used by FS02-030; the final canonical token string is URS §21 OPEN-20. Must agree with `version`, which a validator cross-checks.

version.description: Licence version carried by the repository (GH-022).

published.description: Publication date of THIS licence version — the anchor for the fixed four-year Apache-2.0 conversion clock (D9, FS02-010 `license_pub_date`). The conversion date published on the repo record is derived from it, never stored.

adopted.description: Date the LICENSE commit landed on the default branch (FS02-010 `adoption_date`). Adoption completes on that merge and nothing else (VIS-01), and cannot precede `published`.

text_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the committed licence text, as verified against the published canonical text (GH-015). A modified text is not an adoption (D10).

weight_class.description: Pricing weight class (D11). Lowercase is the frozen form (FS02-010 CHECK constraint); VS-03's `{Standard, Major}` is display capitalisation. The multiplier itself is Schedule-owned and never appears in the registry (FS02-070: admins pick a class, they never enter numbers). Set through the dashboard menu, never by the manifest (APP-029); at v0 by operator-merged pull request.

weight_class_approval_ref.description: Required when `weight_class` is `major`: the public reference (pull request or issue URL) recording the steward approval, so the merge is auditable. `standard -> major` takes effect only on that approval (FS02-071) and merging the record IS the approval being recorded; `major -> standard` is immediate and needs none. The conditional is enforced by the validator, which can express it cleanly.

inbound_family.description: Inbound-licence family of the code the project takes in (FS02-010 `inbound_family`). Drives the FS-09/WEB-034 adoption gate: `permissive` -> notice-preservation instructions; `copyleft` -> declined, manual consent path; `unknown` -> declined to manual review; `none` -> no inbound third-party code. Escrow candidates with copyleft inbound complete the consent path manually or do not qualify (P-M2 §5 item 12).

impact_category_defaults.description: Optional project-level default routing: slugs from the published category menu ONLY (D16, ENG-033 — free text is structurally impossible). Absent means the steward default applies (FS02-050 tier 3). The seven slugs are the categories of the statutes' Art. 7 (D33 item 1); `$defs.categorySlug` is a copy of the enum published in `category-menu.v1.json`, carried here because a published schema must validate on its own download, and asserted identical by the publishing repository's gate.

contacts.description: Curation contacts. LOGINS AND URLs ONLY — no e-mail addresses, no personal names, no phone numbers. This whole repository is data class P0-public (FS-00 §6.9) and person-identifying data beyond a GitHub login plus node_id is out of bounds (D15); the field patterns below make an e-mail address structurally unrepresentable, and the validator additionally scans every string in every record for `@`-shaped text.

admin_logins.description: GitHub logins of the repository administrators the operator corresponded with during curation. Display cache like `owner`/`name`: at P-M3 the claim flow (FS-09) becomes the authority and these are informational.

public_contact_url.description: Optional public contact page or discussion URL for the project.

curation.description: Provenance of this record: how it reached the registry and when. Discovery is a safety net, never the primary channel (FS-02 §4) — `self-registration` is the expected value.

source.description: The channel the record arrived through.

recorded_at.description: UTC ISO-8601 instant the operator recorded this record (FS-00 §6.1: UTC ISO-8601 everywhere). Cannot precede `license.adopted` — the registry records an adoption that already happened (D13).

review_ref.description: Optional public reference (pull request or issue URL) for the curation decision.

repo_url.description: Convenience display link. Derivable from owner/name; recorded so a renamed repository still resolves for a human reviewer.

canonical_of.description: Set on the canonical repository of a fork family (GH-008). Forks are linked, never registered.

notes.description: Curation note for reviewers. Published as part of this public data file, never rendered on a public page.

allOf.$comment: WAIVERS CAN NEVER ENTER THE REGISTRY (FS02-060, D14). Waiver issuance is dashboard-only, by a claimed admin, from P-M3; at v0 the /waivers/* artifacts render the honest empty state. `additionalProperties: false` already rejects these keys, but a bare 'additional property not allowed' error teaches a contributor nothing, so the ban is also spelled out and the validator turns a hit into a named, quotable failure.

Nor may a record carry money, entitlements, contributor shares, or manifest parse results. Those are platform state (FS-05/FS-06/FS-07) or P-M3 surfaces; a PR-curated public YAML file is not where any of them may appear.

githubLogin.description: GitHub's own login grammar: alphanumerics and single interior hyphens, at most 39 characters.

githubNodeId.description: A GitHub GraphQL REPOSITORY node_id, in either of the two forms that exist: the current `R_`-prefixed form and the legacy base64 form, whose decoded value begins `010:Repository`. The pattern narrows the legacy branch to that prefix; the validator additionally base64-decodes and asserts `010:Repository<number>`, which no pattern can do. That check matters because this is the FS02-095 one-node_id-one-registration key: a user or organisation node_id must not pass.

categorySlug.description: The seven published categories of the statutes' Art. 7 (D33 item 1). A copy of `category-menu.v1.json#/$defs/slug`, asserted identical to it by the publishing repository's gate — schemas here are self-contained, so one downloaded file validates on its own and cross-file references do not exist.
